title: Willowbrook ColdChain pilot — field capture & next steps
body:
Context:
Customer: Willowbrook ColdChain (regional refrigerated logistics operator). Pilot scope: replace heuristic rule engine for temperature anomaly detection and delivery ETA chat assistant; evaluate private deployment inside their Azure VNet + edge inference on gateway boxes. Pilot timeline: 8 weeks.

Call attendees (2026-02-18):
- Willowbrook: Priya Kapoor (Head of Ops), Daniel Hsu (Edge SW lead), Omar Aziz (Security), Katalin Varga (Data eng)
- Redwood: Maya Chen (Solutions eng, owner), Jordan Patel ( infra/ops ), Aisha Gomez (security review)

Recording/notes link: https://redwood.internal/meetings/2026-02-18-willowbrook (internal)

High-level ask / success criteria (customer stated):
- Detect temperature excursions within 30s of sensor reading (99% recall for excursions > 2C outside threshold)
- Provide driver-facing chat assistant (on-device) with sub-2s median response time for canned prompts
- Keep PII and route-level shipment metadata inside VNet; no telemetry leaves private deployment except aggregated metrics
- Proof that Redwood private runtime can run on their fleet gateway hardware (NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX-ish) for small LLMs + offload heavy gen to VNet-hosted nodes

Functional requirements captured:
1) Inference types: classification/detector (streaming/online), short-form generation (driver messages), embeddings for similarity (incident grouping).
2) Models: prefer open quantizable model (gpt-small-ish / LLaMA2-7b-q8?) for on-device, larger 13–70b in private cloud for fallback/contextualization.
3) Dataflow: sensor -> gateway preprocess -> local inference -> upstream message bundle every 10 min or immediate on excursion.
4) Observability: token-level cost not relevant for private deploy but need latency histograms, per-device error counts, per-route anomaly rate.

Non-functional / constraints:
- Air-gapped depot sites: some gateways will be offline for long stretches (satellite uplinks). Must support offline inference and eventual sync for logs.
- Fleet hardware: 1 GPU-equivalent on gateway, 4–8GB usable VRAM after OS. Quantization and kernel compatibility are critical.
- Network: intermittent LTE with 1–2s jitter; fallbacks should not block driver UX.
- Compliance: shipment IDs are sensitive; KMS integrated with customer-managed keys (Azure Key Vault) required.

Estimated workload sizing (pilot window):
- Pilot fleet: 25 gateways, 3 depots; peak local QPS per gateway: ~0.5 rps (bursty on pickups)
- Cloud fallback QPS: up to 5 rps aggregated during day
- Token estimate: detector outputs small; driver chat ~20–80 tokens per exchange; embeddings batch every 6 hours per depot (small)

Initial model suggestions (Redwood internal notes):
- Local gateway: 1) tiny quantized causal model for canned responses, 2) lightweight binary classifier distilled from larger model for anomaly confirmation. Target: <2s median on device.
- Private cloud: 13B quantized for contextualization, reranking embeddings with 2–4% QA loss but big cost/latency win.

Gotchas / risks flagged on call:
- Jetson kernel mismatch: several community kernels for q8 ops missing — need trial on dev gateway ASAP. Jordan to validate kernel support and provide a short checklist for customer to collect dmesg + nvidia-smi outputs.
- Data residency: Willowbrook insists on no raw sensor payload leaving the VNet; our agent/collector design must encrypt and redact before any telemetry leaves their control plane.
- Cold-start for anomaly model: will require 7–14 days of baseline data per route; plan for an initial rule-based fallback during warm-up.
- Driver UX expectations: offline mode for chat must gracefully state limited context and queue requests to cloud; avoid hallucinations.

Short-term technical to-dos (owner / by):
- Action: Jordan Patel — prototype q8 kernel run on Willowbrook dev Jetson (get logs). Due: 2026-02-25.
- Action: Maya Chen — deliver architecture sketch (edge + private cloud split) and cost/latency tradeoffs. Due: 2026-02-23.
- Action: Aisha Gomez — prepare KMS integration checklist and RBC (risk-based controls) summary for customer security. Due: 2026-02-26.
- Action: Willowbrook (Daniel) — provide sample anonymized sensor dump + gateway OS image access for compatibility tests. Due: 2026-02-24.

Mid-pilot milestones (proposal):
- Week 1: compatibility tests + baseline data ingestion pipeline (rule-based anomaly ON)
- Week 2–3: deploy quantized tiny model to 5 pilot gateways, run shadow traffic, collect latency/accuracy
- Week 4–6: deploy private cloud contextualization, start online evaluation vs baseline rules
- Week 7–8: expand to 25 gateways, sign-off on SLA targets, handoff ops runbook

Notes on observability + rollback:
- Need per-model canary deployment path and automatic fallback to rule engine if confidence drops below threshold for >1% of events in 1 hour.
- Add a metric for ‘offline-forwarded-events’ count to detect gateways losing connectivity.

Open questions for Willowbrook (to surface next call):
- Can they accept an ephemeral connection to Redwood control plane for deployment orchestration, or must orchestration be fully customer-run?
- Exact KMS policy constraints (can Redwood request re-encryption keys for aggregates?)
- Shipping manifest integration: which fields are considered sensitive PII (customer will check)

Meeting artifacts to produce (Redwood):
- Compatibility report (Jordan) — include kernel logs, model run times on dev Jetson + recommended quant settings.
- Pilot architecture diagram + handoff runbook (Maya) — include sample configs for VNet peering, firewall rules, and KMS policies.
- Security brief (Aisha) — RBC and data flow diagram showing where data is redacted/encrypted.

Immediate next step (this week):
- Internal sync Wed 2026-02-19 10:00 (Maya, Jordan, Aisha) to split tasks and confirm test harness.
- Email customer with onboarding checklist and minimal sample data template by 2026-02-19 EOD.

Freeform notes / heuristics from call:
- Keep local model vocabulary narrow (logistics jargon) to save tokens and improve on-device perf.
- Use prefix caching for route context on gateway; only send compact deltas to cloud to reduce bandwidth.
- Consider fallback to structured responses (templated JSON) vs free text for driver UI to limit hallucinations when offline.

Bottom line: Good fit for Redwood Private + edge combo but hardware compatibility is the gating factor. Early focus: get a dev Jetson running quantized model within the week and lock KMS constraints.

Email to send (draft bullets):
- Recap of call, link to checklist + sample data template
- Proposed milestones and high-level timeline
- Request for gateway image + anonymized sensor dump

-- end of capture --
